Scenario: AiTM Session Hijacking — Partner Account Compromise
corroborated_brief: HIGH CONFIDENCE: Partner developer at DevPartner Inc. account used to clone 3 sensitive repos (phoenix-core, phoenix-api, phoenix-auth) from IP 185.220.101.x (known UNC-XXXX egress point). Developer's credentials appeared in dark web dump 48h prior. Impossible travel detected: US login, then RU-based clone within 20min. CrowdStrike process alert on partner workstation shows Evilginx2 proxy artifact. Three competing explanations remain in play: targeted state-sponsored IP theft, opportunistic credential abuse, or a disgruntled insider. The breach is confirmed, but its downstream business impact on ApexCode's revenue-generating products has not yet been quantified and must be assessed. The actor's follow-on objectives are likewise unassessed and provisional, so a forward monitoring plan is required to define the new signals that would confirm the actor's next moves (searching the cloned code for hardcoded secrets, targeting downstream customers, or weaponizing the code) and that would strengthen or refute the current attribution over time.

HIGH CONFIDENCE: Ransomware (LockBit variant) detected on 3 endpoints in Engineering subnet. Lateral movement via PsExec + stolen service account credentials. Initial access vector unclear. Three possible vectors: (1) phishing email with macro-enabled attachment delivered to engineer 72h prior, (2) CVE-2024-21887 on Ivanti Connect Secure VPN gateway (unpatched, internet-facing), (3) pivot from already-compromised partner VPN session (DevPartner Inc. breach timeline overlaps). 12 endpoints show DNS queries to known C2.
expected_key_finding: VPN exploitation most consistent with evidence timeline

Scenario: Insider Threat — Data Hoarding vs. Legitimate Work
corroborated_brief: MEDIUM CONFIDENCE: Product Engineering employee downloaded 847 files (design docs, customer integration specs, architecture diagrams) over 5 business days. Employee received performance warning 2 weeks prior. All access via corporate VPN during business hours. Employee recently volunteered for cross-team integration project. No external transfer detected. USB policy enforced (blocked). Personal email not accessed from corporate device.
expected_key_finding: Insufficient evidence to determine intent — both hypotheses equally consistent

corroborated_brief: HIGH CONFIDENCE: Malicious npm package 'lodash-utils-extended' (typosquat of lodash-utils) detected in production CI/CD pipeline. Package contains obfuscated post-install script that exfiltrates environment variables (including API keys and deploy tokens) to external endpoint. Three possible injection points: (1) compromised developer workstation pushed poisoned package-lock.json 5 days ago, (2) GitHub Actions workflow YAML was modified to pull from attacker-controlled npm registry for 6 hours before reversion, (3) Artifactory remote proxy may have cached malicious package during brief upstream npm registry compromise.
expected_key_finding: GitHub Actions workflow modification most likely (6-hour window matches exfil timeline)

corroborated_brief: HIGH CONFIDENCE: CFO email account compromised via OAuth consent phishing. Two concurrent threat activities: (1) wire transfer request for $2.1M sent to AP team (intercepted before execution), (2) inbox rules forwarding all emails containing 'acquisition', 'merger', 'board', 'revenue' to external ProtonMail address. Rules active for estimated 12 days before detection. 847 emails forwarded. Competing hypotheses: single sophisticated actor with dual financial/espionage objectives vs. access broker who sold CFO access to two independent buyers. Team consensus is that a single actor is responsible, but this view has not been formally challenged.
expected_key_finding: Single sophisticated actor more consistent — rule creation and wire request within same session
